summary: Peering-authentication bypass to administrative privileges; NETCONF access lets the attacker manipulate fabric configuration; in the CISA KEV catalog.

summary: Second critical unauthenticated peering-authentication flaw found by Rapid7 (coded from the advisory-level description).
notes_B: Peering-auth bypass to admin assumed from "same class as I07"; the cited URL names CVE-2026-76504 (API auth bypass), not CVE-2026-20182. Source/CVE mismatch; C4 either way. Coded from the summary column only; cited source not opened.
notes_B2: Source/CVE mismatch: the cited advisory cisco-sa-sdwan-rpa-EHchtZk is Cisco's advisory for CVE-2026-20127 (I07), and CVE-2026-20182 is in cisco-sa-sdwan-rpa2-v69WY2SW (the cited page itself did not open); Rapid7 and the Canadian Cyber Centre say CVE-2026-20182 is a separate vdaemon peering-authentication bypass giving administrative access and NETCONF, exploited in the wild in limited attacks. This also corrects my first-pass note, which said the I08 URL names CVE-2026-76504; that was wrong.

summary: Manager flaw exploited before disclosure (root access per the research note); management-plane compromise can propagate to downstream edge devices.
notes_B: Mandiant and the Cisco advisory say an authenticated netadmin attacker can run arbitrary commands as root on the SD-WAN Manager by uploading a crafted file (exploited as a zero-day; the "unauth" in the access column is not what the source says). Source: https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/zero-day-exploitation-cisco-catalyst-sd-wan-manager (cited CSA note not opened; Mandiant report used instead).

summary: API session-authentication bypass (URL-encoding handling) gives the admin user on the Manager API; exploited, no workaround.

notes_B2: CVE-2026-76504 is an API session-authentication bypass (URI-encoding handling) that gives an unauthenticated remote attacker admin-user access to the Manager API; Cisco confirmed exploitation in the wild and there is no workaround.

summary: Unrestricted file upload to code execution (VersaMem web shell) that hooks authentication to harvest plaintext credentials; exploited by Volt Typhoon; KEV.

Source: https://thehackernews.com/2024/08/chinese-volt-typhoon-exploits-versa.html and https://vuln.today/cve/CVE-2024-39717 (cited BleepingComputer page not opened).

summary: Improper input validation reaches privileged internal functionality when edge certificate authentication is configured; needs the public part of an edge certificate; KEV.

Source: https://www.securityweek.com/arista-urges-immediate-patching-of-exploited-vco-zero-day/ (BleepingComputer original not opened; syndicated copy and runZero/ionix summaries used).
